title: Baghali Polo
subtitle: broad bean and dill rice
excerpt: Baghali Polo is a fragrant Persian rice dish layered with beans and fresh dill, then steamed with saffron and butter until the base forms a golden crust. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Baghali Polo is a spring dish in Iran, traditionally made with fresh broad beans when they come into season. It is one of the most fragrant of the Persian polo rice preparations.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Persian word for broad beans, the green legume that gives this spring rice dish its name and distinctive earthy sweetness.
The Persian style of cooking rice with layered ingredients steamed together to form a golden crust at the base of the pot.

content.text: comes from layering dill through the rice during the steam phase. The dill wilts into the grains and perfumes every mouthful. This recipe uses haricot beans with the same prep note as broad beans would require. Serves 4.
Serve alongside lamb chops or roast chicken. The rice is substantial enough to be a vegetarian main alongside yoghurt.

items.prepNote: tinned, drained and rinsed; broad beans work very well here

content.text: Bring the salted water to a rolling boil. Add the rinsed rice and parboil for 6 minutes. The rice should be cooked on the outside but still have a slight bite in the centre. Drain through the colander and rinse briefly with cold water.
Heat the oil and half the melted butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Add a 3cm layer of parboiled rice to the base of the pan and press down gently. This forms the base crust.

Mix the remaining parboiled rice with the drained haricot beans and half the chopped dill. Add the rice and bean mixture on top of the base layer, mounding it gently. Scatter the remaining dill over the top.

Drizzle the remaining melted butter and the saffron water over the top of the rice. Poke 5 holes through the rice to the base using the handle of a wooden spoon. Wrap the lid in a tea towel and cover tightly.

Cook over medium heat for 3 minutes until steam rises. Reduce to very low heat and cook for 35 minutes. The base should be golden and crispy. Serve by spooning the rice and bean mixture onto a platter, then unmoulding the crust on top.

attrs.problem: Dill lost its colour and turned olive
attrs.solution: Dill discolours with extended heat. Mix it into the rice just before the steam phase so it is not in contact with the hot oil for long. The shorter the contact with direct heat, the greener it stays.

attrs.problem: No crust formed at the base
attrs.solution: Increase the initial heat slightly and ensure the oil and butter are fully hot before adding the first layer of rice. Press the base rice down firmly. The crust needs direct contact with the hot oiled base.
Check the seal on the lid. Steam must be trapped inside to cook the rice. If the lid is not tight, wrap an extra layer of tea towel around the rim. Add 5 to 10 more minutes of cooking time.

content.text: Baghali Polo is a spring dish across Iran, timed to the arrival of fresh broad beans in the market. The dill and bean combination is one of the most beloved flavour pairings in Persian cooking. It is often served with lamb shank at Nowruz and other spring celebrations. The fragrance of dill steaming inside the sealed pot fills the kitchen before the dish even reaches the table.
